transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-20
Start time: 16:00 PST (23:00 UTC)
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: All-hands (Redwood employees) — Asha, Daniel, Maya, Luis, Rina, Connor + company-wide

Summary:
Asha opens with company health, revenue and usage highlights; Daniel presents infra and performance updates (latency work, KV cache improvements); Maya covers product launches and roadmap (Dedicated improvements, Redwood Optimize pilots); Rina covers sales motion and enterprise wins + pricing changes; Connor discusses hiring pause and benefits adjustments; Q&A follows with cross-functional questions on security, private deployments, and budget.

Topics:
- Company metrics & financials
- Product roadmap: Redwood Dedicated / Private / Optimize
- Infra & performance optimizations
- Hiring pause and org updates
- Sales & GTM motion and enterprise signings
- Q&A and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Asha: hey everybody, welcome, uh, thanks for joining, small ask — we're recording this, recording captioning on, um, quick housekeeping, if you have questions use Q+A and we'll try to get to as many as possible.

[00:22] Asha: quick top line — Q4 finish was solid, revenue up 28% year over year, usage growth in hosted API up ~40% month over month in Dec, we passed 800 customers total, enterprise bookings looked healthy, um, full details in the deck.

[00:40] (laughter) Speaker 1: woohoo, clap emoji in chat.

[01:05] Asha: couple points — margin compression from spot GPU price increases, so you'll see higher infra spend, we're offsetting with Optimize tooling and better batching but it's visible in the numbers.

[01:34] Daniel: yeah hi all — infra update — we've landed continuous KV prefix caching in the runtime which reduces tail latency on repeated contexts, early tests show 15-25% token-cost reduction in common webchat workloads, but there's still some edge cases with long context sequences. some of the kernel selection work is still in flight.

[02:05] Daniel: note — some of this was mis-transcribed in our internal notes as K-V cash, so ignore that haha.

[02:28] Asha: good, thanks. Luis will you give the deeper infra numbers?

[02:34] Luis: sure, I'll pull up the slide — ok, so infra spend increase was about 12% qtr over qtr, but committed Dedicated contracts improved our gross margin for those accounts. public hosted margin slid a bit due to spot pricing. we have a few levers: smarter quantization profiles, smaller instance families for low-traffic models, and improved batching logic.

[03:10] Luis: we've also validated the new kernel selector on A100 and H100, average latency improvements ~8% on H100 for our Llama-variant workloads. there are a handful of odd workloads where latency regresses — we're triaging.

[03:38] Asha: thanks Luis. Maya — product and roadmap?

[03:44] Maya: thanks, hey everyone — product highlights: Redwood Optimize beta is live for 12 customers, seeing immediate cost savings from batching and smart routes; Dedicated product added burst capacity options and canary rollouts; Private early access is on track — a handful of pilots with healthcare and finance customers.

[04:12] Maya: quick note — one pilot had issues with our VPC onboarding script (transcribed as VPC on boarding scrip), turned out to be a doc step missing — fixed now, doc link in the deck.

[04:28] Asha: nice. Rina on GTM?

[04:32] Rina: yeah, Q4 enterprise momentum — three new logos in finserv and one large healthcare pilot (names redacted for NDA). pipeline looks healthy for Q1, but we are asking teams to prioritize expansion plays into existing accounts. also, small change to enterprise pricing: new committed volume discounts for Dedicated customers — details will go to named account teams today.

[05:05] Rina: also to note, competition is getting more aggressive on list price promotions — we need to lean into our reliability and observability story.

[05:30] Asha: ok, hiring and people ops — Connor?

[05:35] Connor: hi all — we are instituting a company-wide hiring pause effective today for non-exempt roles, with a handful of exceptions for critical product and infra work. managers should submit exception requests by next Monday. compensation adjustments: small increase to parental leave and expanded remote stipend. details in the HR doc — I'll follow up with a thread.

[06:10] (clarification question in chat) Speaker 2: question — does hiring freeze affect interns?

[06:18] Connor: interns are included, but internship program lead will be reviewing case-by-case, please route through your manager.

[06:30] Asha: quick financial context — board asked us to be conservative on headcount given near-term macro uncertainty; we made this decision to protect runway while continuing to invest in the areas that drive revenue and retention: infra stability, Dedicated capacity, and enterprise security.

[06:55] (crosstalk) Speaker 3: ok thanks.

[07:05] Asha: now Q&A — please raise hands.

[07:12] Speaker 4 (Eng): hi — question for Daniel, are there any planned changes to our caching strategy that will require model owners to change prompts or tokenization?

[07:25] Daniel: good Q — no changes to model owners needed, the caching is transparent at the runtime layer, though we recommend teams avoid unnecessary randomization of context keys for best hit rates.

[07:45] Speaker 5 (Sales): question for Rina — how's pricing communicated to customers, i.e., will current committed customers get grandfathered?

[07:54] Rina: yes grandfathering for existing contracts, new committed tiers apply on renewal or new contract; we'll be sharing an FAQ and a rollout timeline.

[08:10] Speaker 6 (Security): hi — can we get a status update on SOC 2 and audit logs for Private deployments?

[08:20] Maya: we're on track for SOC 2 Type II evidence collection in Q2, Private deployments already have audit log hooks and KMS integration — one pilot asked for HSM-level keywrap which is being scoped.

[08:40] Daniel: additional note — we're adding more structured tracing in the console so customers can map tokens to requests for debugging; low overhead but very helpful.

[09:05] Asha: ok, a quick product demo preview — Maya, can you show the Optimize dashboard?

[09:15] Maya: sure — (screen share) this is a live beta screenshot, shows route-level cost breakdown, recommended quantization profiles and a suggested batching policy. one thing to call out: recommendations are heuristic and should be validated with your workload.

[09:55] (audio glitch) Speaker 7: uh sorry audio hiccup.

[10:10] Asha: logistically — offsite is April 12-14, travel support available, more info from People in the next week.

[10:22] Speaker 8 (Eng): are we planning any layoffs?

[10:28] Asha: no, this is a hiring pause not layoffs, we want to be explicit about that.

[10:40] (silence) Speaker 9 (Customer success): question about renewals — how are we supporting Dedicated customers during migration windows?

[10:49] Luis: Dedicated customers get a dedicated migration engineer and a 2-week overlap for cutover, we've added an SLA clause for migration windows in the new contract template.

[11:10] Asha: ok, I'm going to call out some wins — shout out to the infra team for getting the H100 rollout stable, the sales team for closing the medtech pilot, and product for launching Optimize beta.

[11:30] (applause) Speaker 10: cheers.

[11:40] Asha: now lightning updates from org leads — 60 seconds each.

[11:45] Maya: product — focusing next 6 weeks on rollout of canary routes and a better observability tab in the console; docs fixes for Private onboarding.

[12:10] Daniel: infra — finish kernel selector rollout, reduce p95 latency by 10% on long-context jobs, finish CI for H100.

[12:30] Luis: reliability — more chaos testing in staging, improved autoscaler heuristics for Dedicated.

[12:45] Rina: sales — prioritize expansion plays, new enterprise comp plan live, named account teams get pricing packet today.

[12:58] Connor: people — hiring pause details in HR thread, career ladder calibrations next week.

[13:15] Asha: final reminders: all-hands recordings and 1-pager will be posted, please read the hiring pause doc and submit exception requests if needed.

[13:30] (Q&A continued) Speaker 11 (Fin): question — do we have a target for gross margin improvement?

[13:40] Luis: target is to recover 300-400bps by Q3 via Optimize adoption and more Dedicated commitments.

[13:55] Speaker 12: question — ok on private deployments and data residency, any changes for EU customers?

[14:05] Maya: we are expanding EU Private region options, will have region-isolated control planes as an option later this quarter, doc and compliance checklist coming.

[14:25] Asha: thank you everyone — last thing, we'll hold a smaller leadership town hall next week for managers to discuss exception flow.

[14:38] (wrap) Asha: thanks all, meeting adjourned.

Notes and links referenced (in chat):
- Leadership deck (link) - will be posted to #all-hands and email
- Private onboarding doc (fixed) - doc link
- Infra cost spreadsheet (internal) - not public

End of transcript.
